clue.text: Gave up and went to bed

definitions.meaning: to hand yourself or something over to the authorities, surrendering it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both surrendering something to the police and retiring for the night.

clue.text: Get run over and call for immediate attention

indicators.note: over in the sense of knocked over and tumbled, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is knocked down by a car and needs help at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns GET and RUN, six letters, into the answer; the definition reads as 'calling for immediate attention'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pressing demands prompt action, which is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Requires that it is unnecessary for the French to leave

indicators.note: the French article is told to go away, so its letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: needless means not required, unnecessary
les is the French plural form of 'the'

explanation.surface: A grammar rule about dropping French articles that are not needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes LES out of NEEDLESS, leaving the four-plus-one letters that remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To require something is to have a want or necessity for it.

clue.text: Enormously upset because south wind went round

indicators.note: the word for 'went' goes round, so it encloses the other pieces

parts.note: went is a euphemism for passed away, died
S is the compass abbreviation for south
a gust is a sudden blast of wind

explanation.surface: Someone is greatly upset because a southerly gale changed direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' is a euphemism for passed away; 'round' has that word split open to hold the south wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgust is strong revulsion, a powerful feeling of being upset or offended.

clue.text: Nicked when spotted around the church

indicators.note: the word for 'spotted' sits around the church, enclosing it

parts.note: spotted means noticed, observed
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A building was cut or chipped when someone saw it near the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicked' suggests stolen, but here it means cut with small marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick is a small cut, and a notch is a small V-shaped cut, so the two verbs match.

clue.text: Grab a few notes

definitions.meaning: a brief fragment of a song or tune

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning to seize hastily and a noun for a short burst of music heard.

clue.text: Stretches up for the photos

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: spans are lengths or stretches of time or distance

explanation.surface: Someone stretches upward to pose for the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SPANS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Snaps is informal for snapshots, quick photographs.

clue.text: Declaration is daft if a six has been made!

indicators.note: made in the sense of formed anew, so the letters are put together in a fresh order

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a statement is silly because a cricketer hit a six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been made' rearranges DAFT, IF, A and VI together.
explanation.definitionFit: An affidavit is a written statement sworn on oath, a formal declaration.

clue.text: Looked after the tea in a cutter

indicators.note: after places the word for 'looked' behind the other pieces

parts.note: cha is a British slang word for tea
saw means looked at, observed

explanation.surface: Someone minded the tea while it was on a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looked after' seems to mean cared for, but it signals the word for 'looked' placed last. A cutter is a tool here, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chainsaw is a powered saw used for felling and cutting timber.

clue.text: Issue of sulphurous material sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the whole run of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
serge is a hard-wearing twilled fabric

explanation.surface: A smelly fabric was returned to the supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue can mean a way out or outflow, which is an exit.

clue.text: Reptile plants a flower

parts.note: the toad is loosely taken as a reptile here, though it is an amphibian
flax is a plant grown for linen fibre

explanation.surface: A lizard puts a bloom in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The toad is an amphibian, but crosswords often loosely call it a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a wild plant with yellow snapdragon-like blooms.

clue.text: By reason of not being out so often

parts.note: in is the opposite of out, as in cricket
as much means to the same degree or as frequently

explanation.surface: A cricketer stays in so frequently that they are never dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means since or because, giving the reason for something.

clue.text: Taking part of the shunting track

definitions.meaning: supporting one side in a dispute
a short railway line off the main route used for parking wagons

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the act of supporting one faction and a short rail spur for shunting.

clue.text: Didn't trouble to invade until a very long time ago

indicators.note: trouble means to disturb or stir up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An army waited ages before getting round to an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges INVADE and UNTIL behind the A; 'Didn't' and 'to' only dress the surface of an army in no hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word literally means before the Flood, so extremely old or from ages past.

clue.text: Sharp-like mineral water

definitions.meaning: somewhat sour or tart in taste
a description of spa water with a tart taste from dissolved carbon dioxide

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means slightly sour, and naturally sparkling spring water is described with it.

clue.text: The sheltered side of a dry well in the east

indicators.note: the letters are put in a different order, mixed in with the extra letter

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A dried-up well stands on the protected flank of a hill in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A DRY WELL plus E are rearranged; the clue has no clear anagram signal, with 'in' doing the work weakly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lee is the side away from the wind, so this means towards the protected side.

clue.text: Confirms what Goldilocks discovered

definitions.meaning: supports or backs up a claim
in the fairy tale she found the family of three animals away from home

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means corroborates, and read literally it says the animals were away from their cottage.

clue.text: Great confusion with a wager about comparatively undomesticated chaps

indicators.note: the word for a wager goes about, surrounding the other pieces

parts.note: a bet is a wager
wilder is the comparative of wild, less tame
men are chaps

explanation.surface: Gambling on which men are the most savage causes bafflement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the wager wrapped round the comparative of wild and the chaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewilderment is a state of complete puzzlement.

clue.text: Made a bit of a noise while stealing cattle

definitions.text: Made a bit of a noise
definitions.meaning: made a soft crackling sound like dry leaves
took livestock unlawfully, the cattle thief's crime

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both made a soft crackle and stole livestock.

clue.text: Drawing of a pointed boat

parts.note: pointed refers to a compass point, here S for south
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A picture shows a boat with a sharp bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointed' looks descriptive but gives a compass point, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing.

clue.text: Hollow depression

definitions.meaning: a channel or low hollow in the ground
a low point, as in a weather system or a cycle

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a long hollow or channel and also a low point such as an area of low pressure.

clue.text: People who entertain large numbers

explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both those who receive guests and great multitudes, as in heavenly armies.

clue.text: Ballet in which star's ankle was broken

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A prima ballerina injures her foot during a famous performance.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Tchaikovsky's famous ballet about an enchanted princess.

clue.text: Garment clung immodestly in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing clings revealingly to the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a cloth wrap worn around the waist in South Asia.

clue.text: There's an enormous disadvantage in using solid fuel

indicators.note: the word for disadvantage goes in the word for solid fuel

parts.note: coal is a solid fuel
a loss is a setback or disadvantage

explanation.surface: Burning solid fuel has a huge drawback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' has the disadvantage tucked into the fuel; 'There's an' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means gigantic.

clue.text: Indicate not to go in the river

indicators.note: go in says the small word is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another in Wales and England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning sign says do not enter the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go in' has the plain word placed in the river; the Dee is a common crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: To signify or point to something is to indicate it.

clue.text: Spots one disturbance in spite of drooping eyelid

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs things up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone has spots and a sagging eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptosis is the medical term for a sagging upper eyelid.

clue.text: Brilliant 24 hour match

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours
a light is something to light a cigarette with, such as a match

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture that lasts a full day is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a sporting fixture but is a light for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad daylight is the brightest natural illumination, hence brilliance.
